title: Bound for an integrated Gaussian density derivative
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\leq1$ for every $z$. Let $v\geq0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. The norm of the integral of $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian density derivative with mean $c$ and variance $v$, integrated against Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, is at most
\[
|I|\left(1+\frac1v\right).
\]
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R^I$, then $\|\int f(z)A_v(c,z)\,dz\|\le|I|(1+1/v)$, in operator norm for the maximum norm.
